acm.realVsHedge.mechanism: Growth measured since the session open separates real accumulation from intraday hedging.

act.condition: operator logged take vs pass on the in-play zone
act.mechanism: Selection quality is a separate skill from read quality; passes are the control group.

decision.mechanism: The matrix earns or loses its cell labels; a cell measured under 45% gets re-worded to skip.

decision.A×A.mechanism: Matrix cell A×A must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.A×B.mechanism: Matrix cell A×B must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.A×C.mechanism: Matrix cell A×C must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.B×A.mechanism: Matrix cell B×A must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.B×B.mechanism: Matrix cell B×B must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.B×C.mechanism: Matrix cell B×C must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.C×A.mechanism: Matrix cell C×A must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.C×B.mechanism: Matrix cell C×B must earn its label from measured outcomes.

decision.C×C.mechanism: Matrix cell C×C must earn its label from measured outcomes.

defl.trigger.condition: closed bar tags the node zone and closes back away from it (✓), or closes through it (✗)
defl.trigger.mechanism: reactionQuality judged the wick every poll and flickered. A latch decided on bar close is the only version of this claim that can be scored the way it was shown.

defl_ant.condition: px within 0.6 of a grade>=B node and approaching
defl_ant.mechanism: Anticipation is geometry, not prophecy — it must still be scored like everything else.

dex.levelNotSign.condition: netDex recorded per bar in $M with the spot it was measured at, to-Friday and 0DTE
dex.levelNotSign.mechanism: Index chains are put-OI dominant so the sign essentially never flips; only the level against its own history can carry information. Non-voting until measured.

dir.condition: directionGrade: SMA-50 trend sets direction, drift confirms or diverges, hard caps override
dir.mechanism: One direction verdict per bar; the hierarchy beats any single input only if A outranks B outranks C.

dir.A.mechanism: Direction A = drift agrees + structure aligned + trending regime; the fusion should follow through.

dir.B.mechanism: Direction B = one leg of the fusion missing or mid-range capped.

dir.C.mechanism: Direction C = chop, mid-range, or opposed structure. No directional claim.

dir.drift.condition: driftRead dir + verdict, scored on its own
dir.drift.mechanism: Drift is only allowed to CONFIRM or DIVERGE, so its stand-alone rate is the honest test of that role.

dir.kingRoll.mechanism: The settlement magnet moving is the board repositioning; whether it LEADS price is an open measurement.

dir.relation.mechanism: The hierarchy only earns its keep if the relation separates outcomes better than the trend on its own.

dir.struct.mechanism: A one-directional factor on a trending day looks like edge; only vote-split vs baseline can tell them apart.

dir.trend5.mechanism: The SMA-50 five-state is the direction; up-broken/dn-broken must earn their own rates before either is allowed to vote.

dir.trendFast.condition: SMA 10 and 20 with the same 15/20 dominance rule, RECORDED not voted
dir.trendFast.mechanism: The 50-period window is an inherited assumption; 10/20 must be measured against it before anything changes.

drift.conf.mechanism: GEX centre and VEX centre on the same side of price with overlapping bands = a real lean.

em.anchoredBand.condition: open from the first RTH candle; EM from dte0 ATM straddle captured once at the open and held fixed
em.anchoredBand.mechanism: The straddle is the market pricing its own day. Anchoring at the open is what lets the band show overextension - recentred on spot it would only ever follow price. dte0 ONLY: toFri holds a later expiry worth roughly double.

em.pace.condition: pct of the straddle travelled divided by √(elapsed fraction of the cash session); not reported below 4% elapsed
em.pace.mechanism: Price diffuses with the square root of time, so half the clock means about 71% of the move is due, not 50%. Without the correction the same percentage means opposite things at 10:00 and 14:30. DESCRIPTIVE: it says the day is running hot or cold against its own pricing, never which way.

em.read.condition: two clauses: where the day is, then the nearest level that changes the hedging mechanism and what it changes to; FLIP outranks piles within 12 points
em.read.mechanism: The section already carries every fact; what it lacked was the causal chain between them. The line states a MECHANISM and never a probability - no likely, no will, no trade - because gamma says HOW price moves and never WHICH WAY, and converting hedging dollars into points needs a market-impact figure the chain does not contain. Which BRANCH fires is recorded so the composition itself can be scored.

exp.breadth.condition: strike present at >= EXP_BREADTH_MIN in n expiry columns; structural = n >= 2
exp.breadth.mechanism: The front expiry pins price today; the later expirations are the walls that survive the close. If breadth separates the two, it belongs in the node grade — by promotion, not by opinion.

flow.perPoint.condition: net GEX of the NEAR-DATED book divided by one point of spot; the expiry window is recorded with the value
flow.perPoint.mechanism: Gamma forces dealers to re-hedge as price moves, and the near book is where that flow lives. Negative gamma trades with the move (feeds it), positive against it (fights it). The size is measurable; whether price arrives is not, so it votes on nothing until scored.

gateHour.mechanism: The blocker on the path to the King behaves differently by time of day.

gex.path.condition: Mag = largest |net gamma| in the window; CR = most call-dominant strike above spot; PS = most put-dominant strike below spot. Verified against a published GEX table: those three rules reproduce its tagged Call Wall, Put Wall and Peak GEX strike exactly, while max call gamma and max call open interest do not.
gex.path.mechanism: The magnet is where dealer hedging is heaviest, so price is drawn to it; the walls are the two edges where a deflection is most likely. Migration is the live part — a floor that rolls up is dealers defending higher. Non-voting until the scorecard earns it.

kill.midrange.mechanism: Mid-range (0.35-0.65 of Flr..Ceil): no edge either way (Skylit midpoint rule).

kill.negGammaWide.mechanism: -gamma node inside a wide/low-exposure pathway: moves accelerate through, they do not deflect.

kill.noConf.mechanism: Neither VEX drift nor structure agrees with the direction: nothing is confirming.

kill.tap3.mechanism: 3rd+ tap of a node: the zone is spent, reactions stop paying.

ledger.touch.condition: in-play node touched; ledger state acm | dec | gone | hold at the touch
ledger.touch.mechanism: A node is respected while dealers are adding to it and abandoned while they unwind. If true, the acm/dec chip is a deflection filter; if not, it is decoration.

leg.dir.condition: leg engine dir/phase (dir OWNED by the SMA)
leg.dir.mechanism: A trend in node terms is magnet → pullback node → magnet. If the phases do not separate outcomes, the model is a story.

leg.handoff.condition: old pullback node/ceiling Dec (m15 ≤ −8% or ≥25% off its session peak) AND a lower node above price building (m15 ≥ +8% or ≥ PB_MIN_PCT)
leg.handoff.mechanism: The roll is a STRENGTH transfer before it is a strike change. If the transfer is visible early, the pullback node can be named before it qualifies; if it is not, this is a story and the count rule is all we have.

leg.magnet.condition: strongest meaningful node in the trend direction, capped at the King
leg.magnet.mechanism: "Price rallies down to the magnet" is a testable claim: either it gets there inside the window or it does not.

leg.pbDetect.condition: a meaningful node APPEARS or GROWS in the pullback zone after a leg
leg.pbDetect.mechanism: The pullback node is the level the user actually trades from; its deflection rate is the whole claim.

leg.pbPredict.condition: RLY phase + an empty zone between price and the last pullback node
leg.pbPredict.mechanism: Pullback nodes appear AFTER the move, so the only honest forecast is the ZONE — and it must be scored as one.

leg.roll.condition: 2 consecutive pullback nodes rolling with the trend = signal, 3 = confirmed
leg.roll.mechanism: Academy doctrine says a rolling ceiling is strong presumptive evidence. This is the local test of that claim.

levels.condition: CR0/PS0 read inside the front expiry column; CR/PS inside the longest-dated bucket present; FLIP = zero gamma on the native node set (absolute basis when the tape carries it); Mag = heaviest strike. Never pooled across expiry columns.
levels.mechanism: MenthorQ's vocabulary computed from our own tape. FLIP (zero gamma) is the regime line (dampening above, amplifying below); CR/PS are the walls; Mag is the pin. Non-voting until the scorecard says otherwise, and CR/PS carry the reach our chain actually has so a one-week wall is never quoted as an all-expiration wall.

map.lean.condition: ceiling and floor transfers rolling the same direction (or one side rolling with the other silent)
map.lean.mechanism: Structure leading the SMA is the user's core observation. Measured as a direction vote in shadow; promotion would let it grade above C when it leads.

map.transfer.condition: a dec/gone node with an acm node on the same side within PB_REACH
map.transfer.mechanism: The rolling ceiling/floor IS the strength transfer. If transfers predict the next move, the Map line earns a vote; if not, it stays descriptive.

netGamma.condition: signed gamma mass sign from deriveFactors, RECORDED not voted
netGamma.mechanism: Net gamma sign describes how moves TRAVEL; whether it also predicts WHICH WAY is unmeasured.

nextStop.condition: rule-based pick: leg magnet → PB target → Map lean node → wall on the King side → nearer wall
nextStop.mechanism: The one forward call the panel makes. If a rule cannot reach ~50% at 30m with n, it is demoted in the picker order; A is earned by promotion only.

nextStop.60.mechanism: Separates a wrong level from a slow one.

node.grade.mechanism: Fresh clean +gamma nodes still growing are where dealer hedging actually defends.

node.grade.A.mechanism: Fresh clean +gamma node building into the tap.

node.grade.B.mechanism: Node good on most inputs but one is stale or opposed.

node.grade.C.mechanism: Spent or bleeding node; reactions are unreliable.

node.pol.neg.mechanism: -gamma nodes accelerate; a deflection there is counter-character.

node.pol.pos.mechanism: +gamma nodes deflect cleanly (dealers sell into strength).

node.rocDay.dn.mechanism: Since-open faders are being unwound; the level is leaving.

node.rocDay.up.mechanism: Since-open growers are real positioning, not intraday hedge noise.

pbEntry.condition: rule-based pick: leg PB (not ✗) → predicted PB zone → last PB → Map pullback candidate → opposite wall; B = leg + Acm + SMA agree + within reach
pbEntry.mechanism: The level to watch for the deflection that sends price to the Next Stop. Never touched = wrong or slow; touched-and-broke = the node failed; touched-and-deflected = the call. Graded nightly by rule/state/polarity; A by promotion only.

pbEntry.60.mechanism: Separates a wrong level from a slow one.

piles.netPolarity.condition: piles from the dte0 book, the band's own window; size and the 20% cut from GROSS gamma; dollars, path sums and the accel/brake label from NET; netFrac below 15% renders BALANCED and votes in neither sum
piles.netPolarity.mechanism: Gross says how much option gamma SITS at a strike; net says what the dealer actually has to hedge. Sizing with gross while signing with net let a 1.2% residual print as a $59M accelerator - measured 84x overstatement. And obstacles drawn on a band that frames TODAY must expire today, or a blend can manufacture neutrality where the two expiries simply disagree.

predictors.condition: time-to-close, bar of day, distances, session range position, PDC relation, event tag
predictors.mechanism: A model cannot find what was never written down; these are recorded from the start and vote on nothing.

reaction.condition: wick rejection at the node while it is not fading
reaction.mechanism: A rejection wick on a node that is still building is the tape confirming the level in real time.

rshuf.condition: >50% of wall keys turned over between feeds
rshuf.mechanism: A wholesale board reshuffle means the old map is void; movement usually follows.

questions.note: POSITIVE gamma, past 100% of the priced move: does price come back toward the open? This is the reversion hypothesis, and the ONLY cell where the face says STRETCHED.

questions.label: Anchored EM band (open ± today's straddle)
questions.note: NEGATIVE gamma, past 100%: does it keep GOING? If it does, marking this as a warning would have been backwards — which is why the face deliberately stays neutral here.

questions.label: Anchored EM band (open ± today's straddle)
questions.note: once the day has been meaningfully BOTH sides of the anchor, does the newer direction hold, or does it rotate again? This is the "goes one way then reverses" case, asked as a question rather than assumed.

questions.label: Anchored EM band (open ± today's straddle)
questions.note: how often does the session actually finish inside anchor ± EM? ⚠ Our band is the RAW straddle = 0.8 sigma, so the honest expectation is ~58%, NOT the ~68% that "expected move" usually means.

questions.label: Pace against the clock (pct / √elapsed)
questions.note: running HOT for the hour in negative gamma: does the day keep going? If pace above 1.2 preceded continuation, a hot reading is a trend tell rather than a warning.

questions.label: Pace against the clock (pct / √elapsed)
questions.note: running HOT in POSITIVE gamma, where dealers damp: does it come back? The mirror claim, scored separately so the two cannot cancel.

questions.label: Pace against the clock (pct / √elapsed)
questions.note: running COLD for the hour: does the session finish inside the band? A coiled day should contain more often than a hot one, and if it does not the chip is decoration.

questions.label: The read (mechanism sentence)
questions.note: when the line says AIR — nothing sizeable between price and the rail — does price actually get there more often than when something is in the way? If not, "air" is a description of the chain rather than a fact about price.

questions.label: The read (mechanism sentence)
questions.note: when a BRAKE is the next thing ahead, does the day stay inside the band? The mirror, and it must be scored separately or the two cancel.

questions.label: The read (mechanism sentence)
questions.note: when the FLIP is the nearest thing, does the forward excursion behave differently from every other branch? This is the strongest claim the sentence makes — that one level inverts the mechanism — and the easiest to falsify.

questions.label: Gamma piles on the band (net-polarised, dte0)
questions.note: more ACCELERATORS than brakes in the band: does the forward excursion get larger? This is the claim the purple markers make visually, asked numerically.

questions.label: Gamma piles on the band (net-polarised, dte0)
questions.note: more BRAKES than accelerators: does the day stay contained? The mirror.

questions.label: Gamma piles on the band (net-polarised, dte0)
questions.note: both dollar figures are on every bar. Does the NET total track forward range better than the GROSS one did? If it does not, the v11.68 fix was cosmetic and should be said so out loud.

questions.label: Hedging flow per point (near book)
questions.note: NEGATIVE gamma, flow feeding the move: does a LARGER flow-per-point precede price actually reaching the expected move? This is the "can hedging carry it there" question, asked rather than assumed.

questions.label: Hedging flow per point (near book)
questions.note: POSITIVE gamma, flow fighting the move: does a larger flow-per-point precede the day staying INSIDE the band? The mirror claim, and it must be scored separately or the two cancel.

questions.label: Net dealer delta (level, not sign)
questions.note: NOT the sign — the sign is pinned. Once there are enough days, does netDex at the rich or flat end of its OWN range precede a directional move, the way the skew read is scored?

questions.label: Gate + hour
questions.note: is the gate reached more in some session buckets?

questions.label: Trend five-state (SMA-50)
questions.note: does 15/20 dominance actually follow through?

questions.label: Trend five-state (SMA-50)
questions.note: does a BROKEN uptrend continue or reverse? (it votes 0 until this answers)

questions.label: Direction input · GEX/VEX drift vote
questions.note: AGREE (overlapping bands) vs LEAN (same side only) — is the overlap worth a whole grade?

questions.label: Direction input · GEX/VEX drift vote
questions.note: UP·conf vs SPLIT realised drift (was the `drift` feature)

questions.label: Trend×drift relation
questions.note: does drift CONFIRMING a trend beat the trend alone?

questions.label: Trend×drift relation
questions.note: does a diverging drift really cost the trend its edge?

questions.label: Direction candidate · net structure tilt
questions.note: on 2026-08-11 structure voted DOWN 46/49 on a down day — is that edge or just the day? (needs the vote-split + baseline columns)

questions.label: Direction candidate · King roll
questions.note: does the King migrating lead price enough to deserve a vote?

questions.label: Direction candidate · net gamma sign
questions.note: does net-gamma sign carry direction, or only volatility character?

questions.label: Direction candidate · faster SMA (10/20)
questions.note: is 50 the right SMA window, or do 10/20 read this tape better?

questions.label: Leg engine · direction + phase
questions.note: does the RLY leg toward the magnet actually travel, or is the phase label cosmetic?

questions.label: Leg engine · pullback-node PREDICTION
questions.note: when the engine names the zone, does a pullback node actually form there within 30m?

questions.label: Leg engine · pullback node DETECTED
questions.note: does a pullback node that ROLLED deflect better than the first one of a leg?

questions.label: Leg engine · rolling pullback nodes
questions.note: after a 2nd / 3rd rolling step, does the trend actually continue DIR_PTS?

questions.label: Leg engine · magnet
questions.note: is the King-capped magnet reached more often than a non-King one?

questions.label: Leg engine · dissipation HANDOFF (old ceiling → new)
questions.note: when the old ceiling is bleeding and a lower one is building, does the named node actually become the pullback node — and how many bars early?

questions.label: Next Stop · reached within 30m
questions.note: does the Next Stop level print within 30 minutes — by rule (leg.magnet / leg.pbTarget / map.lean / wall.*) and by grade?

questions.label: Next Stop · reached within 60m
questions.note: the same call at a 60-minute horizon: how much of the miss at 30m is just time?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: did price pull back to the PB Entry level and deflect DIR_PTS before closing through — by rule (leg.pb / leg.pbZone / leg.lastPB / map.pb / wall.opp) and by grade?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: does an ACCUMULATING pullback node deflect more reliably than a Dec/hold one? (the acm/dec chip earns or loses its job here)

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: −γ pullback nodes: wickier, overshoot-and-reverse — does the touch-then-deflect rule need a wider zone for them?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: does a PREDICTED zone (no node yet) get touched at all within the window?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: do SHALLOW pullbacks (≤50% of the leg) deflect more reliably than deep ones? (a pullback that eats the leg is a reversal dressed as a pullback)

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: does a slow, grinding pullback (low pace, small counterShare, fading last bar) deflect better than a fast impulsive drive into the node?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: does a PB node sitting AT the 50-SMA (±0.2 ATR) deflect better than one far above/below it? and does distance-from-SMA in ATRs grade the stretch?

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: does a FRESH node (born ≤45m ago — dealers stepping in to stop THIS pullback) deflect better than an old level? crossed with rolledFrom/step and m15 (building vs bleeding at the touch)

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 30m
questions.note: 2-3 pullback nodes stacked close together: which one actually turns price — the STRONGEST (highest %King), the DEEPEST (more retracement), or the stack read as one zone? chosenRank tells whether the picker agreed with the answer

questions.label: PB Entry · touched and deflected within 60m
questions.note: the same call with 60 minutes: how much of a 30-minute miss is just time?

questions.label: Expirations · node breadth + structural walls
questions.note: does a node carried by 2+ expirations hold better than a front-expiry-only node? (structure vs a today-level that dies at the close)

questions.label: Expirations · node breadth + structural walls
questions.note: the structural walls are the outer edges of the WHOLE expiry stack — the equivalent of a call/put wall. Does price respect them, and do setups inside the cage behave differently from setups at its edge?

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: THE volatility-level claim: is realised 30m range genuinely smaller ABOVE the FLIP (dealers dampening) than below it (dealers amplifying)? Compare rangeAtr above vs below. If the two are the same, the FLIP is a line we draw for no reason.

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: does price touching Call Resistance actually get rejected DIR_PTS within 30m, or does it walk through? A wall that does not reject is a strike, not a wall.

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: the same for Put Support on the downside.

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: when TODAY'S wall and the STRUCTURAL wall disagree, which one does price respect? crSplit carries the gap in points; compare cr0Defl on disagreement bars against crDefl on the same bars. This is the CR0-vs-CR question and it is the reason the expiry columns get read.

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: does price close at least half the distance to the magnet within 30m more often than chance? Split by magDist so "the magnet is 4 points away" is not scored the same as "it is 0.3 away".

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: price OUTSIDE the structural cage (above CR or below PS): does range expand? This is the trend-day tell if it holds.

questions.label: Levels · CR0/CR · PS0/PS · FLIP · Mag
questions.note: honesty check on our own chain: our CR/PS reaches about a week, not the full chain. Does the one-week wall reject at a rate worth quoting, or is a real all-expiration wall the thing that matters? If this reads at chance, the InsiderFinance lane is worth the grant change; if it reads well, it is not.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: THE user-facing claim — "where price is going". When the structure points at the magnet, does price actually travel DIR_PTS that way within the window? Compare against the tape's own trend hit-rate on the same bars: if it does not beat the tape, the path line is decoration and should be pulled off the face.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: when recent bars move AWAY from the magnet, does the pull still hold? If the disagreeing-tape subset hits at chance while the agreeing subset hits well, the tape is the filter and the magnet only adds a target.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: a pinned read is scored on price STAYING inside +/-DIR_PTS. This exists so the feature cannot win by calling everything pinned on a quiet tape — if pinned resolves true no more often than the base rate of a flat window, it is saying nothing.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: MIGRATION, the live part: when the floor ROLLS UP mid-session, does price follow it? A rolling floor is dealers defending higher. Split by the sign of psDelta — a floor rolling DOWN is the opposite claim and must not be pooled with it.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: the control for path_wall_roll: a wall that has STOOD (psHeldMin large) versus one that just moved. If the standing wall scores as well, migration adds nothing and the extra recording can be dropped.

questions.label: Gamma path · magnet pull, cage position, wall migration
questions.note: when the magnet lies BEYOND the near wall, does that wall break more often than it holds? This is the case where the two readings conflict — a floor to lean on, and a magnet pulling straight through it — and it is the one worth knowing.

questions.label: Ledger · touch by node state (acm vs dec)
questions.note: does a node that is ACCUMULATING at the touch deflect more reliably than one that is dissipating? (the ledger question)

questions.label: Map · node transfer (dec → acm on one side)
